title: Monte Carlo Matchups: Simulating Gujarat Titans Against Different Opponents
dek: What would a season look like if Gujarat Titans played the current league again and again? A Monte Carlo simulation, built on recent head-to-head results, turns matchups into a range of outcomes.
excerpt: Simulating twenty thousand fourteen-match seasons from Gujarat Titans' head-to-head results since 2022 gives a median number of wins and a probability of reaching the usual playoff line. The range is wider than any single season suggests.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: From {{ev:mc-m}} decided matches since 2022, the simulation gives GT a median of {{ev:mc-med}} wins in a fourteen-match season.
It gives them a {{ev:mc-p}} chance of reaching {{ev:mc-cut}} wins, the average total of the fourth-placed side since 2022.
Their most favourable matchup in the inputs is SRH; the least favourable is RCB.

sections.heading: Why Simulate?
body: A single season is one draw from a wide range of possible outcomes. Simulation shows the whole range: how often a side would make the playoffs if the same matchups were replayed many times.
CricField took Gujarat Titans' results against each opponent since 2022, pulled each towards fifty-fifty to allow for small samples, and simulated twenty thousand fourteen-match seasons.

sections.heading: The Range of Seasons
body: The median simulated season gives GT {{ev:mc-med}} wins. They reach {{ev:mc-cut}} wins, the average total of the fourth-placed side since 2022, in {{ev:mc-p}} of simulations.
The chart shows the full distribution of simulated wins.

sections.heading: The Matchups Behind It
body: Their most favourable matchup in the inputs is SRH and the least favourable RCB. The input table lists every opponent's record and the probability used.

sections.heading: What the Simulation Assumes
body: It assumes each match is independent and that head-to-head records since 2022 reflect current strength. Squads change every season, so the inputs are already partly out of date.
The schedule is randomised: five opponents twice and four once, the format used since 2022.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Think in Ranges
body: Gujarat Titans should judge seasons against the simulated range, not against a single expected total.
A season near the median is normal; one at the edges is mostly luck, good or bad.

seo.metaDescription: Twenty thousand simulated seasons from Gujarat Titans' head-to-head results since 2022: median wins and playoff chances.

methodology: Built from the CricField warehouse (Cricsheet ball-by-ball data, regulation innings). Models are fitted on the warehouse itself and described in full here. Generated by scripts/editorial/engine. Win probability against each opponent = (wins + 2.5) ÷ (matches + 5), 2022–2026. Seeded simulation; playoff line = average wins of the fourth-placed side, 2022–2026.
